active_failure_clusters.target_layer: discovery policy / plan compiler / signal policy
active_failure_clusters.evidence: These cases have root_cause_set_recall < 0.85 and/or weighted_explanation_coverage < 0.85, so expected causes are missing from the persisted E4 candidate set; ranking cannot recover candidates that were not discovered.

All three cases still have root_cause_set_recall=1.0 and weighted_explanation_coverage=1.0 but top3_contains_all_major_causes=0 after the Round 10 FIX-M commit. This preserves the merge/composition diagnosis but creates a same-category stall risk.

active_failure_clusters.target_layer: attribution/ranking after candidate-list evidence is captured
active_failure_clusters.evidence: These cases have top3_ok=1 and recall=1.0 but top1_ok=0. That is consistent with an ordering/attribution issue, but the active FIX-D multi_cause discovery cluster blocks a ranking.py recommendation under RULE-C3.

active_failure_clusters.target_layer: canonical E4 candidate-set pruning and representative selection
active_failure_clusters.evidence: root_cause_set_precision_avg=0.754710 remains below 0.85 despite improving from 0.653269 in Round 10; many otherwise passing cases still carry broad non-matching candidate tails.

round_comparison.interpretation: FIX-M was net positive for the top3/precision exit blockers but did not improve multi_cause family top3_rate, and it regressed recall/weighted coverage on MC03 plus interaction over-selection on MC02. The next compliant category is discovery, not ranking.py.
